Resources I used: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61987917/how-do-i-replace-k-and-m-with-thousands-and-millions

```{r}
storms <- read_csv("../data/FINAL_wrangled_storm.csv")

#collapsing some storm events
storms <- storms |>
   mutate(
     EVENT_TYPE2 = fct_collapse(EVENT_TYPE,
                                  Floods = c("Flood", "Flash Flood"),
                                  Winds = c("Thunderstorm Wind", "Marine Thunderstorm Wind", 
                                            "Marine Strong Wind", "Marine High Wind"),
                                  Lightning = c("Lightning", "Marine Lightning"))) 
```

```{r}
#wrangling for damage visualizations

damages_numeric <- storms |>
 separate(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,into = c("value","modifier"),
           sep = "(?<=[\\d])(?=[^\\d.])") |>
  mutate(modifier = case_when(
                              modifier == "M" ~ 1000000,
                              modifier == "K" ~ 1000,
                              TRUE ~ 1),
         result_property= as.numeric(value) * modifier) |>
  separate(DAMAGE_CROPS,into = c("value","modifier"),
           sep = "(?<=[\\d])(?=[^\\d.])") |>
  mutate(modifier = case_when(
                              modifier == "M" ~ 1000000,
                              modifier == "K" ~ 1000,
                              TRUE ~ 1),
         result_crops= as.numeric(value) * modifier)


#dataset with total damages and damages per month for both crops and property per year and per state
#I don't think I actually need per month...
damages <- damages_numeric |>
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE2, STATE, YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    total_property = sum(result_property),
    total_crops = sum(result_crops)
    #per_month_property = total_property/12,
    #per_month_crops = total_crops/12
  ) 

write_csv(damages, "../data/damages.csv")

#total damages for property and crops per year, so combining all the states
total_damages_year <- damages_numeric |>
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE2, YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    total_property = sum(result_property),
    total_crops = sum(result_crops)
  )
  

#damages per state
damages_state <- damages_numeric |>
  group_by(STATE, EVENT_TYPE2) |>
  summarize(
    total_property = sum(result_property),
    total_crops = sum(result_crops)
  )
```

```{r}
#damages visualizations
#graphing for each storm type
#added sub graphs for when there are high outliers so the lower values are more distinct

debris_flow_low_graph <- damages |>
  filter(EVENT_TYPE2 =="Debris Flow", YEAR >= 2000) |>
  filter_out(total_property == "0") |>
 # filter_out(STATE == "CALIFORNIA") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = YEAR, y = total_property, color = STATE)) +
  geom_point() +
  ylim(0, 80000000) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total Cost of Property Damage",
    title = "Property Damage Caused by Debris Flow"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

ggplotly(debris_flow_low_graph)

```{r}
#damages for storms per year

damage_year_graph <- total_damages_year |>
  filter(YEAR >= 2000) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = YEAR, y = total_property, fill = EVENT_TYPE2)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total Property Damage",
    fill = "Storm Type"
  )
ggplotly(damage_year_graph)
```


```{r}
#total property damage per state, showing which storms are causing this

damages_state_graph <- damages_state |>
  filter(!is.na(total_property)) |>
  filter_out(total_property == "0") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = STATE, y = total_property, fill = EVENT_TYPE2)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45)) +
  labs(
    x = "State",
    y = "Total Property Damage",
    fill = "Storm Type"
  )
ggplotly(damages_state_graph)
```
